chapter: Brass bands, Eddie Miller and band stories
title: Tom Brown/Ricky Tom and a Whiteman trombonist
summary: Brownlee cannot place a trombonist the interviewer asks about, and tries to recall another trombonist who played years with Whiteman and passed through Pensacola.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: I was going to ask you about a guy called Ricky Tom, or Tom Ricky. Did you ever know him, a trombone player? He was in and out of town. I never could figure out quite what he was doing, did I?
He was a circus man more than anything else.
He hung around an exchange alley, I think.

I can't truthfully say that I remember him now. I may have remembered him as some other, maybe some other nickname or something like that, but I just can't recall him. I was trying to think of a trombone man that used to play with Whiteman and came back and he came through here in Pensacola and I think he had a few jobs around here, he and Johnny Niles and somebody else. What was that fella's name? He was a very fine trombone player.
No, he wasn't from New Orleans originally, but he played with Whiteman for a number of years, oh many years.
Someone like Billy Ryan, Bill Ryan?
